runs.sql: SELECT count(*) AS old_all_day, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::time <> '00:00') AS old_all_day_off_utc_midnight FROM native_user_availability WHERE is_all_day AND created_at < '2025-12-11';
runs.reading: no all-day witness before the cutoff; the 2025-12-11 cutoff was too narrow (SQL written 2025-12-10, git history from 2026-01-16 already contains the conversion)

runs.sql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM native_rehearsals WHERE created_at < '2026-01-17' OR created_at IS NULL) AS rehearsals_old, (SELECT count(*) FROM native_user_availability WHERE created_at < '2026-01-17' OR created_at IS NULL) AS availability_old, (SELECT count(*) FROM native_user_availability WHERE is_all_day AND (starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::time <> '00:00') AS all_day_off_utc_midnight, (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT user_id FROM native_auth_providers WHERE provider_type = 'email' GROUP BY user_id HAVING count(*) > 1) d) AS users_with_duplicate_email_provider;

conclusions.FM01: No rehearsal or availability row created before 2026-01-17 (or with NULL created_at) survives, so no row that the historical conversion could have shifted remains in place. Limit: a copy re-saved by a client after 2026-01-17 cannot be told apart by these counts.
conclusions.FM02: No user has more than one email-provider row.
conclusions.observation: Two all-day availability rows start off UTC midnight. Every availability row is created on or after 2026-01-17, so these were written by a client after the conversion, not by it. The server does not validate the all-day form (route comment: full slot validation belongs to C02). Writer not yet identified.

nextQuery.purpose: identify the writer of the two rows without personal data
nextQuery.sql: SELECT source, type, external_event_id IS NOT NULL AS imported, to_char(starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'HH24:MI') AS start_utc, to_char(ends_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'HH24:MI:SS.MS') AS end_utc, to_char(created_at, 'YYYY-MM') AS created_month, count(*) AS n FROM native_user_availability WHERE is_all_day AND (starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::time <> '00:00' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 ORDER BY 6;
